newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Dadas H1 net profit falls 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Dadas H1 net profit falls 50 pct.

text.p: Slovenian financial consultancy Dadas said on Thursday its provisional net profit for the first six months tumbled to 42.3 million tolars ($313,000) from 86 million in the year-ago period.
In a statement, Dadas said sales rose to 6.8 billion tolars from 407.5 million.
Following the results, the Ljubljana bourse resumed trading in Dadas after suspending the shares on Tuesday after Dadas shed 53.05 percent the day before, pulling the market to an all-time low.
Dadas stock caved in on market rumours the company may be facing bankruptcy while its brokerage may eventually be banned from trading.

Traders said the better-than-expected half-year results may push Dadas up significantly short-term, although they said most investors have lost faith in the company. In early trade, Dadas was up 10 percent at 14,090 tolars.

Dadas started facing problems in March when the Securities Market Agency initiated procedures to ban its brokerage from trading, claiming it was rigging price by trading among its affiliated companies. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
